To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adherence barriers and facilitators are not limited to drug use; (2) drug use is a barrier to adherence but so are many other factors; (3) drug use does not always interfere with adherence; (4) drug use does interfere with adherence, sometimes in ways not anticipated by clinicians; (5) drug use may not always be a problem for adherence; and (6) drug users are not inherently incapable of adhering to medication regimens.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which adherence and drug use are linked, and how this linkage affects treatment decisions and outcomes.

how adherence is conceptualized and how it is measured, as well as with the implications of stereotyping for HIV care and research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drug use can be, but is not always, a barrier to adherence.
drug use can be a barrier to adherence but it is not the only barrier, and drug use does not always interfere with taking medications as prescribed.
drug use can be, but need not always be, a significant barrier to HAART adherence for drug users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
drug users' adherence is more complex than is often assumed.
the lives and experiences of drug users living with HIV are more varied and complicated than the stereotypical assumptions that underlie the current treatment gap.
adherence is a complicated issue for active drug users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adherence is a complex phenomenon, requiring a more sophisticated understanding of the factors that influence it.
drug users are a heterogeneous group with diverse needs, and that the needs of active users of illegal and legal drugs should be addressed separately and with care.
drug users, like others living with HIV, are not all alike, and that the lives and experiences of active drug users are not necessarily more chaotic than those of non-users.
